hypothesis: The neuron responds strongly to monochromatic or high-contrast grayscale images featuring a central, volumetric, light-colored mass—typically spherical, bulbous, or cylindrical—set against a stark black or deep dark gray background. The activating object, usually white, light gray, or silver, exhibits gradient shading that defines its 3D convex form and frequently displays surface textures such as fur, stippled peel, craters, or concentric ridges. The background is consistently dark and uniform, creating a sharp light-on-dark contrast. The feature typically occupies 30–80% of the image area and is positioned centrally. The neuron remains invariant to the object's semantic identity (e.g., planets, fruit, plastic bottles, animal parts) and surface material, provided the global form, strong contrast, and monochromatic palette are maintained.
